newsitem.title: USA: Santa Fe pours first gold at Mule Canyon.
newsitem.headline: Santa Fe pours first gold at Mule Canyon.

text.p: Santa Fe Pacific Gold Corp has begun gold production from its new Mule Canyon mine in northern Nevada, the company said in a statement Tuesday.
Mule Canyon, acquired in 1993, is part of the Lone Tree Complex, east of Battle Mountain, Nevada, and has reserves of about one million ounces of gold.

"Mule Canyon is a new mine that will help Santa Fe Pacific Gold to meet its projection of being a producer of more than one million ounces in 1997 and approximately 1.25 million ounces in 1998," company chairman Patrick James said.
"In fact we will be very close to producing at a record of one million ounce annual rate beginning in this fourth quarter of 1996," he said.
Mining began at Mule Canyon on October 29, 1996, following the approval by the U.S. Bureau of Land Management for operations to begin.

As of November 22, 1996 the first Mule Canyon gold was included in gold ore poured at the Lone Tree complex, after processing about 3,000 tons of ore at an average grade of 0.57 ounces per ton, he said.
In 1997 about 800,000-900,000 tons of Mule Canyon's ore will be shipped to Lone Tree and the nearby Twin Creeks complex for processing, James said.
Santa Fe Pacific Gold is one of the largest gold mining companies in North America with mines in Nevada and California.
